nota: Biblioteca de «Tu paso de hoy». Se genera; no editar a mano: los pasos propios van en en.json.

pasos.texto: Make a list of five things you like to touch: a fabric, a warm mug, wet soil, an animal’s fur. Underline the one closest to you right now.
pasos.porque: Your body knows small pleasures you almost never write down.

pasos.texto: Remember the last time you laughed until your stomach hurt. Write down where you were, who else was there, and what exactly was so funny.
Think of someone who helped you with something practical: a move, paperwork, a ride. Write down what exactly they did and how you felt when it was done.
pasos.porque: Naming the exact gesture makes gratitude more than politeness.

pasos.texto: Finish this sentence three times, with three different endings: “I feel at peace when…”
pasos.porque: Knowing when you feel at peace helps you look for those moments.

pasos.texto: Think of an activity that makes time disappear without you noticing. Describe the last time it happened and what exactly you were doing.
Describe a meal you remember fondly, from any time in your life: what it smelled like, how it tasted, where you were, and who, if anyone, was with you.
Write about a movement your body enjoys without anyone asking: stretching when you wake up, walking fast, dancing in the kitchen when no one’s watching. Say when you last did it.
pasos.porque: Enjoying movement doesn’t need a goal or a measure.

pasos.texto: Pick an object you use every day, like keys or a mug, and describe it as if you were seeing it for the first time. Note what traces of time it already carries.
Write down what it is about someone close to you that makes you smile: a gesture, a quirk, the way they tell a story. Describe it in enough detail that a stranger would recognize them.
Write about something you did this week that went better than you expected, even if it was small. Walk through how it happened, step by step.
pasos.porque: The small things that went well are forgotten fast if you don’t write them down.

pasos.texto: Finish this three times: “Something I’m curious about and have never tried is…” Pick the ending that surprises you most and write why.
Remember something good that came your way without you planning it: a meeting, a coincidence, a door that opened. Write how it happened and what you were doing that day.
pasos.porque: Noticing what arrived unasked helps you trust what’s coming.

pasos.texto: Describe a place where your body unclenches, real or imagined: what you hear, what it smells like, how the light falls. Write it as if you were giving someone you love directions.
Write God a few lines about your day, the way you would to someone who truly listens: what happened, what you felt, without fixing anything.
pasos.porque: You don’t need pretty words; saying what is there is enough.

pasos.texto: Write down which song moves your body before you decide to: your foot, your shoulders, your head. Say where you were the last time it played.
Remember a recent moment when you felt something bigger than your day: a sky, a melody, a silence. Write it down with all the details you can reach.
Make a short list of the people you can be yourself with without effort, even if it’s just one. Next to each name, note what that person does that makes it possible.
Write your body a thank-you note for something specific it did today: carrying the bags, climbing stairs, getting you through the day.
pasos.porque: What your body does rarely gets a thank-you.

pasos.texto: Describe an ordinary Tuesday you would love to repeat: when you wake up, who you talk to, what you eat, what you do with your hands. Ordinary details only.
pasos.porque: What you want from life often hides in ordinary details.

pasos.texto: Make a list of five small finds that brighten your day, like a free seat, a green light, or an unexpected message.
Think of a decision you made this year that you don’t regret. Write down which of your values was behind it, even if you didn’t name it at the time.
pasos.porque: Your values show more in what you decide than in what you declare.

pasos.texto: Write a letter you won’t send to someone you drifted apart from without a fight. Tell them what you miss and what your life looks like now.
Name something you’ve been avoiding this week: a message, a form, a conversation. Describe exactly which part makes you dread it or put it off.
Write a six-line dialogue between the part of you that wants to rest and the part that wants to keep going. Let them listen to each other and reach an agreement.
Jot down something you assume about someone close to you: what they think, what they want, why they did something. Below it, write the honest question you could ask to check.
pasos.porque: Asking usually costs less than going on imagining the answer.

pasos.texto: Write down what your body has been asking of you for days: to move, to be quiet, to stretch, to stop. Answer it in one sentence, the way you would answer someone you love.
Recall a conversation this week where you spoke harshly or in a rush. Write what you said, how you would have said it with full attention, and what was going on in you just before.
pasos.porque: Seeing what’s behind a word helps you choose the next one.

pasos.texto: Write what you trust today without needing proof: a person, a process, the way things tend to work out. Then say where that trust comes from.
pasos.porque: Knowing where your trust comes from lets you look after it.

pasos.texto: Think of a decision you have pending and note what you gain and lose with each path. End with one line: which path would the version of you that you most admire choose?
Write to God about a decision you’re facing: what weighs on you, what you fear, what you hope for. Then sit for one quiet minute, without needing an answer.
Tell about a time someone said a hard truth to you with care. Write what they said, how they said it, and what you did afterward.
Write about a situation where you said “yes” while meaning “no.” Then add one line showing how a kind “no” would have sounded.
pasos.porque: Practicing the “no” on paper makes it easier to say out loud.

pasos.texto: Write a four-line dialogue: first what you tell yourself when something goes wrong, then what a dear friend who overheard it would answer.
pasos.porque: We often talk to ourselves worse than we would to someone we love.

pasos.texto: Write about a part of you that you rarely show: a talent, a sense of humor, a tenderness. Then name someone with whom it would be safe to let your light show more.
Note where your time went this week: how much went to what truly matters to you, and how much to sheer inertia. Just observe; there’s nothing to fix.
Write down what you need from the people close to you that you almost never ask for out loud, and how you would ask in one simple sentence.
pasos.porque: What goes unasked is almost always waited for in silence.

pasos.texto: Describe how rushing shows up in your body: your jaw, your shoulders, your pace. Then note what time of day it happens most often.
Remember something that didn’t go the way you wanted and led you somewhere you hadn’t planned. Tell how it went, without forcing yourself to find a bright side.
pasos.porque: Looking back sometimes reveals a thread that couldn’t be seen at the time.

pasos.texto: If today feels possible, write about a wound you still carry, only as far as you want. You can stop after the first line; that counts too.
pasos.porque: Putting words to what hurts doesn’t oblige you to resolve it.

pasos.texto: Write a letter you won’t send to someone who hurt you. There’s no need to forgive: tell them what happened, what it cost you, and what you’re not ready to let go of.
pasos.porque: Naming the harm without rushing to forgive is also progress.

pasos.texto: Imagine someone who loves you speaking about you twenty years from now. Write the two things you would like them to say about how you treated people.
pasos.porque: What you want remembered about you points to how you want to live today.

pasos.texto: Finish the sentence “What I fear losing most is…” and write four lines about why. Don’t look for comfort or a solution; just look at it squarely.
pasos.porque: A fear on paper looks clearer than one that only circles in your head.

pasos.texto: Name something you stopped trying for fear of doing it badly. Say what you miss about it and what its smallest possible version would be.
Write four lines of good wishes for someone you have tension with: may they be safe, may they find calm, may they receive what they need. If it won’t come today, write them for yourself.
pasos.porque: Wishing someone well doesn’t oblige you to reconcile or forget.

pasos.texto: Write what gives you meaning on the days that have none: a person, a craft, an animal, a place. Describe one concrete scene that shows it.
Write to God about a pain you still carry, in your own words and without dressing it up, as to someone who listens. You don’t need to end with a conclusion.
pasos.porque: Your pain can arrive just as it is, without tidying up first.

pasos.texto: Write the first line of an apology you might want to give: to whom, why exactly, and how you would say it without justifying yourself. You don’t need to send it today.
pasos.porque: A clear apology starts with knowing exactly what it’s for.

pasos.texto: Think of a time when your light felt very dim. Write what or who held you up then, even if it was something small, and how you would thank them today.
Pick a sentence someone said to you long ago that still echoes in your head. Then write how you would answer it today, in the voice of someone who loves you.
pasos.porque: An old sentence changes weight when you answer it in today’s voice.

pasos.texto: Write down an expectation you’ve carried for years that may no longer be yours: from your family, your work, yourself. What would happen if you set it on the floor for a while?
Do the Morning ritual before you open your messages. The day can wait a few minutes.
pasos.porque: What you do first in the morning sets the tone for the rest.

pasos.texto: Tonight, with the lights low, do the Night ritual before you go to sleep.
pasos.porque: Closing the day on purpose keeps you from taking it to bed.

pasos.texto: When the afternoon gets heavy, stop and do Midday. It takes three minutes to come back to center.
The next time something gets to you today, open “Right Now” before you respond.
pasos.porque: A short pause changes what you say next.

pasos.texto: Pick a line in Anchor and put it where you'll see it today: a note in your wallet or your lock screen.
pasos.porque: What you see often ends up keeping you company.

pasos.texto: Open Affirmations and say out loud the one that's hardest for you to believe. Slowly, three times.
Before bed, write down in Good things something that went well today and what made it possible.
pasos.porque: Knowing why it went well helps you notice it more often.

pasos.texto: Open Free writing and write for five minutes without fixing anything. Whatever comes out is fine.
Read one Story today, unhurried, and keep a single line with you for the rest of the day.
Play a Sound landscape for ten minutes while you do something with your hands, no screen.
pasos.porque: Busy hands and a quiet mind get along well.

pasos.texto: Tap “Make your own,” build today's phrase, and use it as your motto until tonight.
If something in today's letter spoke to you, save it. That way it's close at hand in your Journal.
In Anchor, open the Psalms tab and read one softly, like someone talking with God.
pasos.porque: The psalms give words to what we sometimes can't say.

pasos.texto: Do one full guided meditation, start to finish, with notifications off.
Do the morning Manifestation with a statement you truly want for your life.
Halfway through the day, do Midday standing up, next to a window.
pasos.porque: Changing your posture changes the pace of the day too.

pasos.texto: When you're standing in line or waiting, open Anchor instead of social media and read one line.
pasos.porque: Waiting can be a breather too.

pasos.texto: Do the Architect check-in: what worked this week, what didn't, and what you'll adjust.
Open Vision and write a single line under “Be”: who you want to be this year.
pasos.porque: A written intention is easier to remember.

pasos.texto: Read what you've saved in Good things over the last few weeks and notice what keeps coming back.
pasos.porque: What keeps coming back tells you what's worth protecting.

pasos.texto: Do the Night ritual and, as you let the day go, wish well to someone you clashed with today.
Do the Morning ritual and, in your “If today brings… I will…” plan, choose the hardest moment waiting for you today.
pasos.porque: Deciding ahead of time leaves you less at the mercy of impulse.

pasos.texto: Before the hardest conversation you have today, open “Right Now” and do the full pause.
In Affirmations, tap “My content,” write one of your own, and read it before you head out.
pasos.porque: Words you choose yourself feel more like yours.

pasos.texto: In Free writing, write out the conversation you haven't dared to have, the way you'd like it to go.
pasos.porque: Rehearsing it on paper takes some of the weight off.

pasos.texto: Tonight, turn off screens half an hour before bed and let a Sound landscape play while you get ready.
Read a psalm in Anchor and rewrite the verse that spoke to you most in your own words, as a prayer.
Open Journal › Letters, reread the one that has stayed with you most, and share it with someone who needs it.
Do a meditation somewhere new today: a bench, a park, a quiet corner at work.
Complete all three Manifestation sessions today: morning, afternoon, and night, with the same statement.
Read a Story and retell it to someone today in your own words.
pasos.porque: Telling something is the best way to keep it.

pasos.texto: Reread your whole Vision and change one line that's no longer true for you.
pasos.porque: What you want changes too, and that's okay.

pasos.texto: Take your time with the monthly Architect check-in and choose one thing you'll let go of this month.
In the Night ritual, when the moment to let go comes, let go of an old hurt. Even if it's just for tonight.
pasos.porque: Letting go isn't approving of what happened; it's putting it down.

pasos.texto: In Free writing, write a letter to someone who is no longer in your life. You don't need to send it.
Find a hard day in Good things when you still wrote something down, and read it slowly.
pasos.porque: Remembering that good and hard coexist gives you solid ground.

pasos.texto: Read a psalm of lament in Anchor and pray it for someone who is going through a hard time.
Call or text your mom, or someone who cared for you like a mother, and tell them one specific thing you're grateful for. If she's gone, write it for yourself.
Today, thank your dad, or someone who was a caring figure in your life, for one specific thing. If that isn't possible, write it for yourself.
Tell someone you love, in specific words, what you value about the way they are.
pasos.porque: Specific words are remembered far longer than general ones.

pasos.texto: Make a small space to remember someone who died: a photo, a candle, their favorite food, a song.
Today, in the middle of the gathering or the quiet, find someone who's on their own and spend a while with them.
Before the year ends, write down one thing you learned and one thing you want to leave behind.
Choose a single word for this year and write it where you'll see it every morning.
pasos.porque: One word fits into any day, even the hard ones.

pasos.texto: Today, on Easter Sunday, share some good news from your life with someone, however small.
On the full moon of Vesak, do an act of generosity no one sees: leave something good for someone, unsigned.
pasos.porque: Giving without being known is dana in its simplest form.

pasos.texto: While the water heats up for your coffee or tea, stand and watch it, without touching your phone, until it's ready.
pasos.porque: Waiting without doing anything is a luxury we almost never allow ourselves.

pasos.texto: Pick a task that takes under two minutes and that you've been putting off, and do it now, before moving on to anything else.
pasos.porque: Keeping a small promise to yourself is a way of trusting your own word.

pasos.texto: When you hear someone laugh, on the street, in a video or in the next room, stop for a second and let it rub off on you.
Look at the sky for a minute without taking a picture. Notice what color it is right now and how the clouds move, if there are any.
pasos.porque: Most of the time we only look at the sky to see if it will rain.

pasos.texto: Pray for a minute for someone you see often and barely know, like whoever works at your corner store or drives your bus. Just bring their face before God.
While you brush your teeth, lean on the sink and shift your weight onto one foot, then the other, slowly.
pasos.porque: It fits inside a minute you were already spending, without costing you any time.

pasos.texto: On the way to your first stop today, ask yourself what you're after there, beyond the fact that it's expected of you. Answer in one sentence.
When you finish something today, even something small, wait ten seconds before moving on to the next thing. See that it's done.
pasos.porque: Noticing what you've already done changes what you expect of yourself.

pasos.texto: Make yourself something to eat that you really crave, even if it's just toast with something on top, and put it on a plate.
Before bed, look out a window or from a balcony and find the moon or a star. If it's cloudy, look anyway: there's far more up there than you can see.
When someone rings you up or helps you today, say “thank you” looking them in the eye, not at your phone or the receipt.
pasos.porque: With eye contact, the thank-you reaches a person, not a counter.

pasos.texto: The next time you get up from your chair, do it slowly and feel your feet press into the floor before you take the first step.
pasos.porque: Our feet are almost always left out of our attention.

pasos.texto: Close the tabs and apps you're not using today, and leave open only what serves what you're about to do in the next hour.
pasos.porque: Whatever you leave open keeps asking for a little attention.

pasos.texto: If you feel rushed at some point today, stop where you are and say to God in your own words, “I'm here.” Stay a few seconds in silence.
Use something today that you're saving for an occasion: the good mug, your favorite clothes, the perfume. Today is the occasion.
pasos.porque: Saving the good stuff for later sometimes means never using it.

pasos.texto: Remember something good that happened to you that you didn't plan, and tell someone in your family or a friend about it in a single sentence.
pasos.porque: Sometimes life arranges things better than we planned.

pasos.texto: While you wait in line or at the stop, practice metta toward whoever is near you: repeat silently, “may you be safe, may you be at peace.”
Take your shoes off for a moment and set your bare feet on the floor, the grass or the dirt. Notice the texture of what you're standing on.
Before you pay for something today, ask yourself whether it's for care, for pleasure or for duty. There's no wrong answer; just notice it.
When the next notification arrives that isn't urgent, leave it unopened until you finish what you're doing.
pasos.porque: Almost nothing that buzzes on your phone needs an answer right away.

pasos.texto: Before the task or conversation that weighs on you most today, put it into words before God, in one sentence of your own, no formulas.
When you eat today, think about the hands that brought it to your plate: whoever grew it, hauled it, sold it. Two or three people is enough.
If you see someone in your building or on your street carrying something heavy, offer a hand once. If they say no, that's fine.
pasos.porque: Offering just once leaves the other person free to accept.

pasos.texto: When you lie down, bring your attention to the weight of your body on the mattress, from your heels to your head, without changing anything.
Go through your to-do list and delete one thing you no longer care about. It's allowed to go without you doing it.
pasos.porque: Removing what no longer matters makes room for what does.

pasos.texto: Turn off whatever is making noise at home, like the radio, the TV or a video, and give yourself a minute with the quiet that's left.
pasos.porque: Sometimes background noise weighs more than it seems.

pasos.texto: Rest your hand on a tree, a stone wall or the ground, and stay a minute feeling that something holds you up.
Put on a song you like and move along with it until it ends, even if it's just standing in the kitchen or the hallway.
In your next conversation, let the other person finish their whole sentence before you start yours. Notice whether you wanted to interrupt.
pasos.porque: You listen differently when you're not rehearsing what you'll say.

pasos.texto: Today take the stairs for just one floor, or get off public transit one stop early, whichever is easier for you.
Before you say something important today, ask yourself three questions: is it true, is it useful, is it kind? If any answer is no, wait a moment.
Tonight, before you turn off the light, leave your phone charging away from your bed, on another table or in another room.
pasos.porque: That way the last thing you see today isn't a screen.

pasos.texto: Check today how much money you have available, the way you'd check the weather: no judgment, just to know where you stand.
pasos.porque: A number you know weighs less than one you only imagine.

pasos.texto: Today, between one task and the next, make something with your hands that serves no purpose: sketch, fold paper, mold clay, build. Five minutes is plenty.
pasos.porque: What you do just for the pleasure of it needs no excuse.

pasos.texto: Before your first meal today, quietly thank God for one specific thing that's on your table.
Stretch like a cat waking up: arms overhead, long spine and a yawn if one comes. Do it right where you are.
pasos.porque: Your body often asks to stretch long before you listen.

pasos.texto: Tidy one single drawer, shelf or folder, the smallest you have, and keep in it only what you actually use.
pasos.porque: One finished drawer is worth more than a whole room half done.

pasos.texto: On your next trip, put your headphones away and listen to the sounds around you: engines, footsteps, voices, a door beeping.
Tonight, pick out tomorrow's clothes, the ones that feel most like you, and leave them where you can see them.
Go somewhere daylight reaches you, a yard, a sidewalk, an open window, and spend two minutes there without your phone.
pasos.porque: A change of place, even a small one, already changes the day.

pasos.texto: Watch something that changes while you look at it: the light on a wall, a cloud, the shadow of a branch. Remember that everything moves like this.
pasos.porque: Watching something small change helps you accept the big changes.

pasos.texto: Greet someone who lives near you by name, or ask what they're called if you don't know. That's enough for today.
pasos.porque: Knowing the name of someone nearby changes the greeting.

pasos.texto: Think of someone who benefits from what you do today, whether it's work, study or caregiving, even from afar. Keep their face in mind as you start.
Wash your hands today paying attention to the water: its temperature, the soap, the moment you rinse. Don't do anything else meanwhile.
The next time someone asks how you are, answer with one word that's true, even if it isn't “fine.”
pasos.porque: A small truth, said in time, saves a lot of explaining later.

pasos.texto: Do something small for someone without telling them, like straightening their chair or leaving a kind note. That's how your light reaches somewhere nobody expected it.
Water a plant, or put a bean in a cup with damp cotton. Remember that something grows without you pushing it.
Tell someone in your family, your home or your work “thank you for…” and finish the sentence with something specific they did today.
At your next meal, make the first bite screen-free: chew slowly and notice the texture and the flavor.
pasos.porque: One bite with attention already changes what eating feels like.

pasos.texto: Before you start working or studying, spend a minute with your hands on the desk and your eyes on one spot, not doing anything yet.
pasos.porque: Starting without hurry changes how what follows feels.

pasos.texto: Ask for one small thing today: the time, directions, someone to pass the salt. Notice that asking didn't break anything.
Do a small act of generosity today (dana): give something without expecting anyone to notice, like a coin, your place in line or a piece of fruit.
Notice something today that works without anyone thanking it: the water from the faucet, the light bulb, the solid floor. Pause a moment in front of one.
pasos.porque: What we take for granted is almost always held up by someone.

pasos.texto: Send a friend a photo, a song or a meme that made you think of them. No long text; that's enough.
pasos.porque: Small and frequent keeps people closer than big and rare.

pasos.texto: Rub your hands together until they warm up, then rest them for a moment over your closed eyes.
Before you sleep, quietly ask yourself one question: what wants to grow in me? Don't answer it; let it spend the night with you.
Say out loud something you do well, from cooking to listening. Say it all the way through, without adding a “but.”
If there's someone in your family who's easy to talk to, ask them about a dish that reminds them of childhood, and listen to the whole story.
pasos.porque: Recipes hold stories that almost no one has asked about.

pasos.texto: Before opening your email or morning messages, decide on the one thing you'd like to have done by tonight.
pasos.porque: Choosing before you open your messages keeps others from choosing for you.

pasos.texto: If the path allows it, walk one block at half your usual speed and look up: rooftops, wires, branches, the sky.
Message someone you work with today and tell them exactly what they did that made your week easier. Give a real example, not a “thanks for everything.”
pasos.porque: Most people never find out what actually got noticed.

pasos.texto: Next time someone in your family does something that irritates you, ask “What happened?” before you reach your own conclusion.
pasos.porque: There's almost always a part of the story you don't know.

pasos.texto: Call today to book that checkup or appointment you've been putting off. Just book it; going is a problem for another day.
pasos.porque: With the date set, the rest is just showing up.

pasos.texto: Ask the right person for one concrete thing you need to work better this week: a piece of information, more time, a schedule change.
pasos.porque: Nobody can give you what they don't know you need.

pasos.texto: Answer that message from a friend you've been leaving for later. Two lines are enough, even if it feels late.
Look at one charge or subscription you don't remember choosing. Decide whether it stays or goes, and make the change now.
pasos.porque: Choosing with open eyes is not the same as paying out of habit.

pasos.texto: Accept an invitation today that you would normally let pass, without knowing how it will go or what you'll find.
pasos.porque: You don't always know in advance what will matter to you.

pasos.texto: Before a conversation that's hard for you, pray for a minute for the person you're about to talk to. Ask God to help you listen to them.
Mute the group chat that drains you most until tonight. The messages will still be there when you decide to open them.
Greet a neighbor by name, one you only ever nod at. If you don't know it, ask.
Say a kind “no” today to something you'd normally accept out of obligation: “Thanks for thinking of me, I can't this time.”
Invite someone to walk with you for twenty minutes today: at lunch, after work, or around where you live. Name the day and the time.
Before anything else, give ten minutes to the task you've dodged most this week. After that you can move on to everything else.
pasos.porque: Starting weighs more than continuing; the ten minutes usually stretch.

pasos.texto: In any conversation that gets tense today, practice right speech: say only what is true and useful, and let the rest go.
Tell whoever serves you today, at the register, a counter or a delivery, one specific thing they did well, looking them in the eye.
Tell someone you trust about a doubt of faith you haven't said out loud. Listen to what they say without needing them to settle it.
Pay back that small debt today, or return what someone lent you. No long explanations: “Sorry for the delay, here you go.”
pasos.porque: A small loose end weighs more than it's worth.

pasos.texto: Tell your partner, or the person closest to you, one concrete thing you need this week, without waiting for them to guess it.
pasos.porque: Nobody guesses well; asking out loud saves misunderstandings.

pasos.texto: Ask the right person for what your body has been asking for at work: a different chair, a mid-morning break, a real lunch hour.
pasos.porque: What isn't asked for almost never shows up on its own.

pasos.texto: Before walking into a place where you tend to shrink, remember one thing only you bring. Go in with your light, without asking permission.
Suggest a plan to someone you haven't seen in a while, with a day, a time and a place, all in a single message.
pasos.porque: A “let's get together sometime” almost never turns into a date.

pasos.texto: Offer to teach someone new at your work or in your group, in twenty minutes, something that took you a while to learn.
pasos.porque: What cost you time to learn saves someone else the trip.

pasos.texto: Today, when someone asks “How are you?”, answer with something truer than “fine,” even if it's just one different word.
Spend ten minutes tidying the one corner that weighs on you every time you see it: a shelf, a drawer, a chair piled with clothes.
pasos.porque: What you avoid looking at keeps taking up space in your head.

pasos.texto: Each time a worry shows up today, set it before God in one sentence and go back to what you were doing.
Ask an older person you know to tell you what an ordinary day was like at your age. Listen without interrupting.
Tonight, charge your phone outside your bedroom and use another alarm clock, even an old-fashioned one.
If you see someone carrying something heavy or looking lost today, ask if they need help. If they say no, take it at face value and move on.
pasos.porque: Offering without insisting is both helping and respecting.

pasos.texto: Ask someone you trust what gave them strength in their worst season. Listen to the answer without comparing it to your own.
Practice dana, generosity, today: give some of your time without expecting anything back. Help with a load, listen without checking the clock, or give up your seat.
If someone served you really well in the last few days, write to their manager or the company and tell them, with a name and details.
pasos.porque: Praise that reaches the person who decides carries different weight.

pasos.texto: In the next meeting or group conversation, give your opinion in the first ten minutes, even a short one.
pasos.porque: Speaking early usually costs less than gathering courage until the end.

pasos.texto: Cook something simple today for someone else and share it with them, no special occasion needed.
Pick one small gesture you want to make a habit and attach it to something you already do without thinking, like pouring coffee or brushing your teeth.
pasos.porque: Something new holds better when it hangs on something you already do.

pasos.texto: Tell someone today something you admire about who they are, not what they achieve. They may not even know it shows.
Write to someone who knows about the thing you've been stuck on and tell them exactly which part isn't working.
pasos.porque: A concrete question gets answered fast; a vague one doesn't.

pasos.texto: If a conversation heats up today, ask for a pause: “I need ten minutes and I'll be back.” Then come back.
Today, if you're with other people and your body is asking you to stop, eat or stretch, say so out loud instead of putting up with it.
Instead of tapping “like” on a post from someone close to you, send them a direct message about what they shared.
pasos.porque: A message of your own feels different from a tap on a screen.

pasos.texto: Think of the thing you left half-done and decide today: either give it ten minutes to pick it back up, or let it go on purpose.
pasos.porque: Letting go on purpose weighs less than abandoning it without deciding.

pasos.texto: Thank someone today who taught you something about your faith, in person or in writing. Tell them what is still alive in you.
Write to a relative you haven't spoken with in months, just to ask how they are. You don't have to bring up what's unresolved.
Do that errand you've put off for weeks before noon today: renewing a document, answering an official letter, returning something to a store.
pasos.porque: What you put off takes up more room in your head than on your calendar.

pasos.texto: Ask today about a trial class for something you feel shy about trying: dancing, swimming, climbing. Just ask; signing up is optional.
Pick one object that has run its course in your life. Remember that everything changes, thank it for what it gave you, and give it away, recycle it or toss it today.
Show someone you trust something you're working on, a draft, an idea or a sketch, before it's ready, and ask what they think.
pasos.porque: What you show half-finished can still be improved in time.

pasos.texto: If something a neighbor does bothers you and you've been turning it over for days, tell them calmly, starting with “It would help me if…”
pasos.porque: A neighbor can't change what they don't know bothers you.

pasos.texto: Trade a few words today with someone you don't know, in line or on the bus: a simple comment, a question, then listen to the answer.
This week, ask a food pantry, shelter or local group near you whether they need a hand, and offer one specific hour.
Today, end your workday at the time you set for yourself, without the usual “five more minutes,” and leave the loose ends written down for tomorrow.
pasos.porque: A limit only works when you keep it, even a small one.

pasos.texto: Ask someone you admire how they knew which path to take. Then tell them where you are right now, without dressing it up.
Cancel or postpone one commitment you keep only out of duty and that costs you more than it gives. Tell them with one honest sentence.
pasos.porque: Every “yes” to what you don't want is a “no” to something else.

pasos.texto: Offer an older neighbor, or one who lives alone, to bring something back from the store when you go out. Make it specific: “What can I bring you?”
Spend ten minutes wishing metta to someone who is difficult for you: “May you be safe, may you be at peace.” Even if you feel nothing today.
If you make a mistake today that affects someone, tell them quickly with an “I got it wrong” and say how you'll fix it.
pasos.porque: Saying it fast costs less than carrying the fear of being found out.

pasos.texto: Think of someone you owe an apology. Tell them what you did and that you're sorry, in one sentence and without adding a “but.” If speaking isn't possible, write it for yourself.
pasos.porque: With no “but” attached, an apology is heard whole.

pasos.texto: Pick an old argument you keep winning in your head and close it: say out loud “I'm leaving this one here,” then do something with your hands, like cooking, washing dishes, or building something.
pasos.porque: Replaying it a thousand times doesn't end it; deciding to close it does.

pasos.texto: Think of something you're often asked for and no longer want to give: time, money, being on call. Pick a short sentence, “this is where I stop,” and say it without explaining. If you can't yet, rehearse it aloud.
pasos.porque: A clear limit protects both of you better than a resentful yes.

pasos.texto: Put a hand on the part of your body you've criticized most and tell it, quietly: “Thank you for carrying me this far.” Stay like that for a minute, without fixing anything.
pasos.porque: Your body carries you every day, and you almost never thank it.

pasos.texto: Do something useful for the people who share your street or building without letting them know it was you: sweep the entrance, pick up litter, straighten a sign. Don't mention it afterward.
Write to or call someone who helped you years ago and never knew how much: tell them what changed in your life because of what they did. If they're gone, say it out loud or write it for yourself.
pasos.porque: Some people never find out how much they meant to someone.

pasos.texto: Name before God someone you find hard to forgive, without asking God to change them or erase what happened. Tell God honestly how far you can go today. There's no need to say anything to that person.
pasos.porque: Saying how far you can go is more honest than pretending you've arrived.

pasos.texto: Choose a truth you've kept from someone and say it today with care: first what you value about them, then what you need them to know. If there's no way to say it, write it down and keep it.
pasos.porque: A truth said with care leaves more room for listening.

pasos.texto: Pick a memory that still hurts and sit with it for five minutes, something warm in your hands. You don't have to understand it or solve it. If today is too much, leave it for another day.
Plant something that will take years to give shade or fruit: a tree, a seed, a cutting in a pot. Do it without knowing whether you'll see it grow.
pasos.porque: Planting with no guarantees is a way of trusting what's coming.

pasos.texto: Without waiting to be asked, do a chore for an older person that is hard on their body: carrying groceries, changing a lightbulb, moving a piece of furniture. If they ask what they owe you, tell them it's nothing.
Write to someone you let down when they were going through something hard and tell them: “I wasn't there when you needed me, and I'm sorry.” No explanations, and nothing asked in return.

Sit for five minutes and, thinking of someone who is hard for you, silently repeat: “May you be free from suffering.” If it won't come today, start with someone easier; wishing someone well doesn't oblige you to get closer.
pasos.porque: Wishing someone well isn't approving of what they did.

pasos.texto: Today, learn the name of someone whose work holds up your day without you noticing (whoever cleans, delivers, cares for, or checks you out) and thank them for one specific thing they do.
Write down on a piece of paper an expectation about your life you've carried for years and ask yourself whose it was. If it's no longer yours, tear the paper up calmly.
pasos.porque: Some goals reach us inherited, without our ever choosing them.

pasos.texto: Ask today for the specific help you've been handling on your own for a long time. Say how much you need and when: “Can you help me Saturday, for an hour?”
pasos.porque: A precise request is easier to accept than a vague “I need help.”

pasos.texto: Think of a meeting, a group chat, or a person that leaves you drained every time. Decide on one concrete limit: a time to leave, a shorter visit, notifications on silent. Protecting your light includes choosing where you place it.
Think of someone who hurt you and pick one small part you can let go of today: a grievance you repeat, or a scene you replay. Letting go doesn't mean talking to them or saying it was okay.
pasos.porque: Forgiving all at once often stays in words; forgiving in parts becomes real.

pasos.texto: Fix something today with your own hands that has been broken for a while and that someone else uses every day: the door that sticks, a zipper, the wobbly chair. Don't announce it; just let it work.
pasos.porque: Repairing with your hands is a quiet way of caring.

pasos.texto: Sit for a while beside someone who is going through a loss or an illness, without trying to cheer them up or fix anything. Listen, and if silence comes, let it be.
pasos.porque: Sometimes what people appreciate most is that someone stays.

pasos.texto: Tell God plainly and in detail about something you owe someone an apology for. Then choose the day and the way you'll offer it, even if it's in writing.
Ask an older person about a hard time they went through and what carried them. Listen to the whole answer, without comparing it to yours and without giving advice.
Step away today from a commitment that no longer makes sense for you (a role, a group, an inherited habit) and let people know with respect and thanks for what it was.
If there's a mistake of yours that no one has noticed, at work, in a group, or at home, tell whoever it affects today and offer a way to repair it.
Take an object you've kept from a relationship that ended, or from someone who's gone, and decide calmly what to do: keep it with affection, give it away, or let it go. Any choice is fine.
Before saying something difficult today, ask yourself three things: is it true, is it necessary, and can I say it kindly? If all three answers are yes, say it.
Choose a time you let down someone younger than you (a child, a niece, a student) and tell them calmly: “That was wrong of me.” Then listen to whatever they want to answer.
Cancel a commitment you'd only attend to avoid looking bad, let people know with one kind sentence and no invented excuse, and use that time to rest without a screen.
Pick something you keep blaming yourself for and say out loud what you'd tell someone you love who had done the same. Then stay a moment, listening to yourself, without arguing back.
pasos.porque: We tend to treat others with more tenderness than ourselves.

pasos.texto: Congratulate someone whose success made you envious, with one sincere sentence and no irony. If it doesn't come yet, write down what that envy showed you about what you want.
Pick something you always handle yourself because you don't trust it to turn out the same, and hand it to someone else today. If they do it differently, don't correct it.
pasos.porque: Some things turn out fine even when they turn out differently.

pasos.texto: Ask someone you love, with whom there was distance and now there's trust, “Can I give you a hug?” If they say yes, make it a long one, the kind no one rushes. If not, that's fine too.
There's something you've spent years waiting to turn out the way you imagined. Tell God, in your own words, that you're handing it over today, and stop planning, for today, how it should be resolved.
Practice dana, giving freely, in secret: give something today (food, time, help) so that no one knows it was you. And when you finish, let go of the tally of what you gave.
pasos.porque: Generosity weighs less when it carries no signature.

pasos.texto: Walk to a tree, a river, or a patch of open sky and say out loud an old expectation that no longer serves you. Leave it there and come back a different way.
pasos.porque: With a sky overhead, letting go costs a little less.
